texts: The main benefit of retrograde cerebral perfusion over selective antegrade perfusion during deep hypothermic circulatory arrest is flushing debris and air out of the cerebral circulation.
Cold blood pushed backwards through the superior vena cava washes particles and air out of the arch vessels into the open arch.
Retrograde perfusion gives the brain little nutrient flow, so it is used with deep hypothermia and short arrest times; antegrade perfusion feeds the brain better and allows warmer temperatures.
Retrograde perfusion is simple to set up, but that is not its principal benefit.
In the picture, cold water is pushed up the chimney into the head lantern and washes grit and soap bubbles out into the open arch.
Memory hook: backwards up the chimney, it washes more than it feeds.
